title: Stream LLM Response From Workflow: 2026 Platform Guide
summary: Stream LLM response from workflow to relay tokens in real time rather than waiting for completion. Compare platform capabilities.
body_markdown:
## Platform-by-platform Verdicts for Streaming LLM Output


Because its docs describe a streamed chat response, n8n ranks first. Windmill and Activepieces are unconfirmed, and Temporal, Airflow, Zapier and Make run the LLM step but need something else to stream it to the caller.


### n8n verdict


Only one pairing here has docs confirming that tokens reach the caller while the run is still going: n8n's Chat Trigger, which documents a streaming response mode, fed by the AI Agent node. The canvas below shows the shape of it, with a test conversation in the chat panel:


- a chat trigger
- an AI Agent node
- an OpenAI chat model
- a memory sub-node


It also shows a failure in the Simple Memory sub-node, which is a reminder that memory is a separate dependency and can break while the model call works.


Pick n8n if the caller is a chat widget or a front end you control. Check that your own flow actually uses the trigger's streaming mode rather than waiting for the run to end, because the default doesn't stream.


### Windmill verdict for streaming LLM output


If your steps are real scripts, you can write the LLM call yourself and return output incrementally, and that is the appeal of Windmill, a developer-first platform. Its docs cover streaming from scripts and an AI agent step in flows.


Treat the HTTP behavior as the thing to test before committing: confirm that the endpoint your caller hits relays the stream rather than returning a finished job result. Pick it if your team is happy writing code and wants self-hosting.


### Temporal and Airflow verdict for LLM streaming


Neither tool documents token streaming to a caller, and Temporal runs durable workflows whose activities return when they finish. Airflow schedules batch tasks, and a task's output lands after the task completes.


Both are good at running the LLM call reliably, with retries and recorded state.


To stream, the activity or task must push tokens to a side channel you build, such as a message broker or a WebSocket service. Pick them when reliability matters more than the live feel, and accept that you own the streaming layer.


Activepieces avoids that second system for the work around the model, though not for the streaming itself.


Its flow builder takes an Agent step and a deterministic step in the same flow, and the run trace records both as a single execution, start to finish, rather than two engines bridged by a callback.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it, but its docs still don't confirm tokens reaching the caller, so that trace argues for background AI steps, not a live chat window.


### Zapier and Make verdict


Run an AI step on either platform and the answer comes back when the run ends. Their webhook-response features return a result at the close of the scenario or Zap, not a token stream.


I found no documented streamed HTTP or chat response in either platform's docs, so a long catalogue of AI actions doesn't change the verdict.


Run the LLM step here if the rest of the automation lives there, and stream from a separate service in front of it.
